candidate_case.canonical_answer: Hold the starter until the engine starts, for a maximum of 5 seconds, provided the starting setup is satisfied. If no start within 5 seconds, release and wait about 5 seconds before another attempt. Do not keep holding the starter for long periods: this can drain the battery below 10 V. An unresolved no-start condition requires authorised-service inspection. Before an actual starting attempt, establish neutral and neutral lamp glowing, ignition ON, right-hand kill switch RUN, adequate fuel/no continuously blinking final bar, clutch pulled in and held, and side stand fully retracted. If you have already made three successive cranking attempts, wait 15–20 seconds for the battery to recover.
